name: feature-to-pr
description: Feature to pull request for NYCFarmerMarkets: drafts and (after approval) creates a GitHub issue, branches from origin/main, plans with a reviewed design loop, records the spec and an issue comment, implements with a review loop, runs build/test/convention gates, opens a PR after approval, then watches and responds to feedback until merged or closed.

steps.prompt:
Step 1 of 8: draft and create the GitHub issue for a new feature.

Project facts: SwiftUI iOS/macOS app at {{workdir}}; Xcode project NYCFarmerMarkets.xcodeproj, scheme NYCFarmerMarkets. Run every git command as `git -C {{workdir}} ...` and use absolute paths everywhere. Fixed task directory for this run's working files: {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/ (never stage or commit anything under .agents/).

GitHub facts: repo iyepes/NYCFarmerMarkets (PUBLIC), remote origin over https, default branch main. The GitHub CLI gh is installed and authenticated as iyepes (scopes repo, read:org, gist); pass --repo iyepes/NYCFarmerMarkets to gh commands. Never work on or push to main; never force push.

Feature: {{feature}}
Optional longer description file (may be empty; read it if non-empty): {{details_path}}

1. Prepare the task directory: `mkdir -p {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr`, then delete stale files from earlier runs in it so no old gate or PR file can stop a loop early: design-review.json, code-review.json, test-gate.json, pr.json, respond.json, test-report.md, and 01-requirements.md, 02-design.md, 03-design-review.md, 04-plan.md, code-review-agent.md, code-review-semantic.md, code-review-summary.md, issue-draft.md.

2. Draft the issue from the feature (and the details file if given): a clear GitHub issue title, a description, and acceptance criteria as a checklist. Derive a kebab-case slug (lowercase, a-z 0-9 and hyphens, at most 40 characters). Write the draft to {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/issue-draft.md (title on the first line, then the body) and keep the slug in your message.

3. PAUSE FOR USER APPROVAL before creating anything on GitHub: call send_message with sessionId 'parent' and severity 'warning', showing the complete draft (title, description, acceptance criteria, slug) and asking the user to approve or request changes, then wait. Remember the repo is PUBLIC. If the user asks for changes, revise the draft, rewrite {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/issue-draft.md and ask again. Do not run `gh issue create` until the user has approved.

4. After approval, create the issue: `gh issue create --repo iyepes/NYCFarmerMarkets --title "<title>" --body-file <body file>` (put the body, without the title line, in a file under {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/). Do not add labels.

Your FINAL message must carry exactly: the issue number, the issue URL, and the slug (for example `issue: 12`, `url: https://github.com/iyepes/NYCFarmerMarkets/issues/12`, `slug: my-feature`). Later steps read it.

Step 2 of 8: create the feature branch.

Project facts: SwiftUI iOS/macOS app at {{workdir}}; Xcode project NYCFarmerMarkets.xcodeproj, scheme NYCFarmerMarkets. Run every git command as `git -C {{workdir}} ...` and use absolute paths everywhere. Fixed task directory for this run's working files: {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/ (never stage or commit anything under .agents/).

GitHub facts: repo iyepes/NYCFarmerMarkets (PUBLIC), remote origin over https, default branch main. The GitHub CLI gh is installed and authenticated as iyepes (scopes repo, read:org, gist); pass --repo iyepes/NYCFarmerMarkets to gh commands. Never work on or push to main; never force push.

Issue details (issue number, URL, slug) from the issue step: {{issue.output}}

1. Make sure the working tree is clean: `git -C {{workdir}} status --porcelain` must be empty (ignore nothing except untracked files under .agents/). If it is not clean, do not stash, reset or discard anything: call send_message with sessionId 'parent' and severity 'warning' listing the dirty files and ask the user how to proceed, then wait.

2. `git -C {{workdir}} fetch origin`, then create and switch to `feature/<issue-number>-<slug>` from an up-to-date origin/main: `git -C {{workdir}} switch -c feature/<issue-number>-<slug> origin/main --no-track`. If that branch already exists, stop and ask the user (warning) instead of reusing or deleting it. Never work on or push to main.

3. Verify `git -C {{workdir}} branch --show-current` prints the new branch and `git -C {{workdir}} rev-parse HEAD` equals `git -C {{workdir}} rev-parse origin/main`.

Your FINAL message must carry exactly the branch name and the base commit sha (for example `branch: feature/12-my-feature`, `base: <sha>`). Later steps read it.

Step 3 of 8 (plan): review the design. You are the gate writer of the design loop.

Project facts: SwiftUI iOS/macOS app at {{workdir}}; Xcode project NYCFarmerMarkets.xcodeproj, scheme NYCFarmerMarkets. Run every git command as `git -C {{workdir}} ...` and use absolute paths everywhere. Fixed task directory for this run's working files: {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/ (never stage or commit anything under .agents/).

Project conventions: all colors only from AppPalette tokens and all icons only from the AppIcon registry (no Color(...) literals, hex literals, or raw SF Symbol names outside NYCFarmerMarkets/Theme/); new files in the NYCFarmerMarkets/ folders are auto-included (synchronized groups, no project file edits); pure logic types are `nonisolated`; Swift Testing for unit tests, XCTest for UI tests; specs live in .kiro/specs/<feature-name>/ as requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md.

Review the design at {{artifacts.design}} against the requirements at {{artifacts.requirements}}. Verify the design's claims about existing code against the actual source in {{workdir}}; do not take its word. Write the full review (numbered findings with HIGH/MEDIUM/NIT severities and concrete fixes, plus Verified Assumptions and Unverified/Wrong Assumptions sections) to {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/03-design-review.md, then the gate file {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/design-review.json as {"verdict": "APPROVED" | "CHANGES_REQUESTED", "findings": [...], "reviewDoc": "<absolute path of the review document>"} with reviewDoc {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/03-design-review.md. The verdict is mechanical: any HIGH or MEDIUM finding means CHANGES_REQUESTED; zero means APPROVED.

Convey your verdict only by writing {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/design-review.json. When you finish, always call send_message with severity 'success', whatever the verdict.

Step 4 of 8: record the plan as a spec, comment on the issue, and commit the spec.

Project facts: SwiftUI iOS/macOS app at {{workdir}}; Xcode project NYCFarmerMarkets.xcodeproj, scheme NYCFarmerMarkets. Run every git command as `git -C {{workdir}} ...` and use absolute paths everywhere. Fixed task directory for this run's working files: {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/ (never stage or commit anything under .agents/).

GitHub facts: repo iyepes/NYCFarmerMarkets (PUBLIC), remote origin over https, default branch main. The GitHub CLI gh is installed and authenticated as iyepes (scopes repo, read:org, gist); pass --repo iyepes/NYCFarmerMarkets to gh commands. Never work on or push to main; never force push.

Project conventions: all colors only from AppPalette tokens and all icons only from the AppIcon registry (no Color(...) literals, hex literals, or raw SF Symbol names outside NYCFarmerMarkets/Theme/); new files in the NYCFarmerMarkets/ folders are auto-included (synchronized groups, no project file edits); pure logic types are `nonisolated`; Swift Testing for unit tests, XCTest for UI tests; specs live in .kiro/specs/<feature-name>/ as requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md.

Commit hook: a PreToolUse hook reviews staged Swift files for security issues before any `git commit`. Expect it to run, honor its findings (on a high-severity finding do not commit: stop and tell the user), and when it passes, run the commit again with exactly the same parameters.

Feature: {{feature}}
Optional longer description file (may be empty; read it if non-empty): {{details_path}}
Issue details (issue number, URL, slug) from the issue step: {{issue.output}}
Feature branch (feature/<issue-number>-<slug>) from the branch step: {{branch.output}}

1. Confirm you are on the feature branch from the branch step (`git -C {{workdir}} branch --show-current`); never commit on main.

2. Write the spec to {{workdir}}/.kiro/specs/<slug>/ (slug from the issue step): requirements.md from {{artifacts.requirements}}, design.md from {{artifacts.design}}, tasks.md from {{artifacts.plan}} (keep the unchecked `- [ ]` checkboxes). Tidy formatting only; do not change substance.

3. Post a concise summary of the plan (key requirements, design approach, the task list) as a comment on the issue: write it to {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/issue-comment.md and run `gh issue comment <issue-number> --repo iyepes/NYCFarmerMarkets --body-file {{workdir}}/.agents/tasks/feature-to-pr/issue-comment.md`.

4. Commit only the spec: `git -C {{workdir}} add .kiro/specs/<slug>` then `git -C {{workdir}} commit -m "docs: add spec for #<issue-number> <slug>"`. Record in the commit message body what you did (files written, issue comment posted).

Your FINAL message must carry the spec directory path and the commit sha.
